author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260513T175453Z-2820386
text:
Escalating to human: this bead asks for a foundation-API change
(`JmapBackend` or a new `SubscribeBackend` trait) that propagates
through the 8 canonical extension-server siblings per workspace
AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule. The API shape is a genuine
design choice with non-equivalent options; per AGENTS.md "Planning"
this needs explicit approval before code touches `jmap-server`.

## Three coupled beads, not one

JMAP-cf7p.9 (signal-driven push), JMAP-cf7p.10 (SSE Last-Event-ID
replay), and JMAP-cf7p.12 (WS pushState replay) are explicitly
described by their own descriptions as a "coordinated cluster" that
share infrastructure: a backend surface that can both (a) wake an
SSE/WS poller on mutation and (b) replay missed state changes after
reconnect. Doing .9 in isolation builds the wake-up half but leaves
the replay half stranded; both halves want the same change-log
surface.

Recommendation: re-shape the three follow-ups into a single epic
with foundation-trait + 8 extension-template + 1 testjig-consumer
child beads. .9 / .10 / .12 collapse into that epic's testjig-
facing children.

## Design options for the foundation surface

Three non-equivalent shapes I considered:

### Option A — default-impl method on `JmapBackend`

```rust
trait JmapBackend {
    fn subscribe_state<O: JmapObject>(
        &self,
        account_id: &Id,
    ) -> impl Stream<Item = State> + Send {
        // default: polling fallback via get_state.
        // Concrete backends override with watch/broadcast wiring.
        polling_fallback(self.clone(), account_id.clone())
    }
}
```

Pros: matches the `principal_id` precedent (default-impl seam,
backends override when they wire it). No new trait. Existing
`MemoryBackend` keeps working unchanged because the default polls
exactly as today.

Cons: `impl Stream` in a default method body needs `async-stream`
or a hand-rolled wrapper; the workspace AGENTS.md TLS-stack-style
preference for narrow dep surface argues against pulling
`async-stream`. The polling default still costs CPU; the only win
is "production backends can override" — which is the kit's whole
point.

### Option B — separate `SubscribeBackend` trait

```rust
trait SubscribeBackend: JmapBackend {
    fn subscribe_state<O: JmapObject>(...) -> impl Stream<...>;
}
```

Pros: keeps the read-side `JmapBackend` minimal; subscribe is opt-in.
The testjig requires `B: JmapBackend + SubscribeBackend` and the
production deployments that don't wire push get a compile error
rather than silent polling.

Cons: 8x duplicated propagation across the extension-server
canonical-template siblings (each needs a `SubscribeBackend` impl
on its `MemoryBackend`). Two-trait pattern is more surface area
than one-trait-with-default.

### Option C — keep `JmapBackend` untouched, add `subscribe()` only on each concrete `MemoryBackend`

The testjig downcasts / casts to each concrete `MemoryBackend` to
get the subscribe handle, no trait change. No workspace-wide
propagation; only `crate-jmap-testjig` and the 8 `memory.rs`
modules change.

Pros: zero foundation-trait surface change. No SemVer churn.

Cons: violates the bead's "Workspace-wide: signal API is added in
a shape consistent with the canonical extension-server template"
acceptance criterion. Future production consumers (kith, stoa)
re-invent the API per-backend.

## My recommendation

**Option A** if the workspace is willing to depend on `async-stream`
(or equivalent) in `jmap-server`; otherwise the cleanest shape is
**Option A with `tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<()>`** as the
subscription value type:

```rust
trait JmapBackend {
    /// A receiver that fires whenever any state token in this account
    /// advances. Default impl returns a never-firing receiver; SSE/WS
    /// pollers fall back to polling against `get_state` when the
    /// receiver never fires.
    fn subscribe_state(
        &self,
        account_id: &Id,
    ) -> tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<()> {
        let (_, rx) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(());
        rx
    }
}
```

Rationale: `watch::Receiver` is already in the workspace's dep
graph via tokio. No new dep. The subscriber `.await`s on
`changed()` and then re-snapshots `get_state` for each tracked
type — same diff machinery as the current SSE polling, just woken
on signal instead of timer.

Replay (cf7p.10/.12) is a separate concern with its own design:
either grow `get_changes_since(monotonic_id)` or extend the
`watch` carrier from `()` to a state-snapshot type. That's the
next-level question once Option A vs B vs C is settled.

If the answer is "do it as one epic, recommended Option A with
`watch::Receiver<()>`", I'll file the epic + child beads (8
extension propagations + testjig consumer + replay design) in the
next session.
